overview: A relay is an electrically-controlled mechanical switch: a small coil, energized by a safe low-voltage logic signal, physically pulls a metal contact closed (or open), letting a microcontroller control circuits at voltages and currents it could never touch directly — mains-powered lamps, motors, heaters. Most breakout modules add an optocoupler between the control pin and the relay coil, electrically isolating the microcontroller from the switched circuit entirely, which matters a lot when the switched side is mains voltage: a fault on the high-voltage side has no direct electrical path back to the microcontroller.
simpleSummary: An electrically-controlled switch that lets a small microcontroller safely control high-power devices like lamps.

specifications.switchedVoltage: Often rated up to 250VAC / 30VDC on the relay contacts themselves
specifications.switchedCurrent: Commonly 10A rated (check the specific relay's datasheet)
specifications.isolation: Most modules include an optocoupler between logic input and relay coil

pinMap.name: IN
pinMap.function: Control input — typically active LOW on common modules (LOW energizes the relay).
pinMap.currentLimit: N/A (drives an optocoupler/transistor, not the coil directly)
pinMap.gotcha: Many modules are active-LOW, the opposite of what beginners expect — double-check before assuming HIGH means 'on'.

pinMap.name: VCC
pinMap.function: Power for the relay coil and control circuitry.

pinMap.name: COM
pinMap.function: Common terminal of the switched (high-voltage) circuit.
pinMap.voltageRange: Up to the relay's rated switching voltage
pinMap.currentLimit: Up to the relay's rated switching current
pinMap.gotcha: This side of the module can carry mains voltage — treat it with the same respect as any exposed mains wiring, entirely separate from the logic side.

pinMap.name: NO
pinMap.function: Normally-open switched contact — connects to COM only when the relay is energized.

pinMap.name: NC
pinMap.function: Normally-closed switched contact — connects to COM by default, disconnects when energized.

useCases.title: Mains-powered appliance control
useCases.scenario: Turn a lamp, fan, or other mains-powered device on/off from a microcontroller, with full electrical isolation.

useCases.title: High-current DC load switching
useCases.scenario: Switch a motor, solenoid, or other DC load drawing more current than a transistor alone would comfortably handle.

useCases.title: Fail-safe circuit design
useCases.scenario: Use the NC contact so a circuit defaults to a safe state if the controlling microcontroller loses power.

oftenConfusedWith: Solid-state relays (no moving parts, faster switching, different failure modes)
oftenUpgradedTo: Solid-state relays for high-cycle-count or fast-switching applications
